source.title: Seeing What Tastes Good: Revisiting Multimodal Distributional Semantics in the Billion Parameter Era
source.authors: Dan Oneaţă; Desmond Elliott; Stella Frank

record.tranche_reason: The study discusses cross-modal convergence and reports correlations between models' attribute-probe performance profiles, but it does not measure representational distances or alignment between paired image and caption representations as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports probe performance on semantic attributes, but those scores alone do not measure representation alignment. Figure 2 and its discussion report pairwise correlations between models' per-attribute probe performance; these are recorded as related findings, not as direct tests of any listed version. Prior alignment results cited in the paper are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study trains linear probes for semantic attributes on frozen encoders. It then correlates per-attribute probe performance between models (Figure 2). That measures agreement in which attributes are easy or hard to decode, not alignment of representations of paired data. It is a related but different construct. Untrained Random SigLIP's profile also correlates highly with trained models (McRae .70–.83, Binder .80–.92), so the profile correlation is largely driven by attribute difficulty. It cannot show representational convergence. The authors frame it as convergence evidence, but no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that multimodally trained vision encoders slightly outperform unimodal ones at attribute probing. Self-supervised Swin-V2 rivals LLMs. Same-modality models correlate more strongly, suggesting somewhat complementary views. High overall correlations are read as convergence comparable to nearest-neighbour findings (Huh et al.).
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear probes to predict semantic attributes and correlates per-attribute probe performance across models; it does not apply the original representation-alignment measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: Vision, multimodal and language encoders have highly correlated per-attribute probe performance profiles, with modality clusters. Mostly .84–.98 for trained models, but .70–.92 even for an untrained random encoder.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different encoders, across modalities, find the same semantic attributes easy or hard to linearly decode. This similarity is substantially driven by attribute properties, since even random encoders share it.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The reported correlations concern attribute-probe performance rather than direct representation alignment. The paper notes that linear probes assume attributes are linearly encoded and that the experiments are limited to English concepts.
record.rows_left_out: Probe performance values in Tables 2 and 5 and per-attribute probe results were left out because they do not measure alignment or similarity between models. Correlation-matrix cell values in Figure 2 were not extracted individually; the paper's textual summary of the aggregate pattern is recorded instead.

untested.parts: No measure of representational alignment versus model scale or capability.
No alignment measure between image and caption (or concept-word) representations, and no trend with model quality.
No feature or circuit recurrence analysis.
No comparison of alignment metrics or input distributions.
No test of plateau or of shared-data explanations of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The authors' convergence interpretation is not supported as a test of V2. The Random SigLIP baseline shows the correlation metric is high even without learned representations, and the authors do not discuss this. Probe accuracies (Tables 2, 5) are correctly excluded as rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether representational alignment rises with model scale or capability.
Does not measure alignment between representations of paired images and captions, or whether such alignment rises as both models improve.
Does not compare independently trained seeds of the same architecture or measure shared features or subspaces.
Does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment between models.
Does not test recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Does not compare representation-alignment measures, their settings, or input distributions.
Does not test whether representation alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: Model pairs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Calculated pairwise Pearson correlations between models' per-attribute probe performance.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between per-attribute probe performance across model pairs
rows.value: The models form modality clusters; the paper describes correlations among reasonable models as generally high.
rows.note: This is agreement in attribute-probe performance profiles, not a measure of representational distances or alignment.
rows.check: Value can be made concrete from Figure 2 (McRae×THINGS). Trained-model pairs mostly correlate .84–.98. Within-vision pairs reach .96, and the CLIP image vs PaliGemma/SigLIP block reaches .96–.98. Untrained Random SigLIP correlates .70–.83 with the others, which gives a baseline. Construct is probe-difficulty profile, not representation alignment.

rows.value: The models form modality clusters; the paper describes correlations among reasonable models as generally high. Swin-V2 correlates more highly with language models on this dataset.
rows.note: The study also notes cross-modal correlations, including the Swin-V2/language-model pattern, but this metric concerns probe-performance profiles rather than representation geometry.
rows.check: Value can be made concrete from Figure 2 (Binder). Trained-model pairs mostly correlate .81–.98. Untrained Random SigLIP correlates .80–.92 with the others, so a random encoder is nearly as 'convergent' as trained ones. Construct is probe-difficulty profile, not representation alignment.
